T-2432 (design Sec2.5): one entry per geometry site the four grounding/temper/audit/fold passes found. `family` is R1 (re-derives hidden_size==num_attention_heads*head_dim), QOW (uses hidden_size as a stand-in for q_proj's/o_proj's true width), or KLP (assumes one K-landing path). `status` is fixed, confirmed-correct, rejected (a defined convert/load-time rejection, not a code fix), or not-yet-built (a Track this build did not own). GS-01..GS-04, GS-06..GS-19 are Track A's own scope (T-2432); GS-05 is Track B's (D-SLM5243), out of this ticket's scope and not yet built. GS-26/GS-27 (T-2441) are RunGreedyDecodeLoop/RunGreedyOrDampedGreedyDecodeLoop's own num_attention_heads threading (Critical 1, D-SLM5431). `required_tokens` (T-2441, S2 fix, D-SLM5436): for a `fixed` site, the literal substring(s) that must appear within that occurrence's own bounded scope (see `required_token_scopes`, below) -- shared across every occurrence of a site (OR semantics, see `require_all_tokens`), never a per-occurrence-distinct value, so re-keying how an occurrence is IDENTIFIED never has to touch this field. Present ONLY on `fixed` sites: `confirmed-correct` sites are intentionally unchanged by this ask (their own governing quantity is correctly hidden_size/intermediate_size, not q_width), so a presence check would be backwards for them, and `not-yet-built` sites have no code to check yet. Derived once, by reading each site's own diff against v1.3.0 (2f225fc..327ee29) -- see tools/geometry_site_census.py's own module docstring for how the census applies this field. `require_all_tokens` (T-2445, default false/absent): when a site's own required_tokens are ALTERNATE spellings of the same quantity at different occurrences (the default, OR semantics -- any one satisfies), this stays false/absent; when a site's ONE occurrence governs several independent sub-assignments that would otherwise share one generic token (GS-18), this is true and required_tokens holds one EXACT fragment per sub-assignment (AND semantics -- all must be present, so reverting any one is caught by that one fragment going missing).

`required_token_scopes` (T-2481, Claude/Mendeleev/t2480-census-recommissioning-2026-08-31.md F1, D-SLM5647/D-SLM5659; replaces `required_token_scope_end_offsets`, T-2475): a map from relative file path (forward slashes) to a LIST of scope records, `{"anchor": <str-or-null>, "offset": <int-or-null>}`, one record per physical marker occurrence of that gs_id in that file (or fewer, when two occurrences share literally identical local code and an identical offset -- see the GS-12 note below). At check time, census.py identifies WHICH record applies to a given physical marker by its own local CONTENT, not by its ordinal position among the site's other occurrences: a record's `anchor`, when not null, is an exact literal substring expected somewhere within that record's own claimed window, `[marker_line, marker_line + offset]`; a null anchor applies only when this gs_id has exactly one physical occurrence in this file (nothing to disambiguate against -- a population of one has no meaningful order to reorder). `offset` is unchanged in meaning from the prior scheme: the OFFSET, in lines, from that occurrence's own marker to the LAST line of that occurrence's own governed code, or `null` if that occurrence has no independently-revertible code of its own (a declaration whose own text never changes regardless of what a sibling occurrence assigns it -- GS-08's forward_sites.h occurrence, and GS-19's own cbuffer-comment occurrence, whose offset is null and whose own `anchor` exists purely to let a physical marker resolve to the right record).

This is the third keying this field has carried, and each of the first two was defeated by an edit its own author did not imagine. `required_token_scope_ends` (T-2445, `"relative/path.ext:marker_line"` -> absolute end line) was ruled self-detecting on the reasoning that census.py recomputes the LOOKUP key's marker_line fresh every run -- true, and irrelevant, because the STORED key and end line were both absolute line numbers frozen at authoring time, so an edit anywhere ELSE in the file (one comment line at the very top, nowhere near any marker) shifted the marker's own current line without shifting the registry to match, producing a false MISSING/mismatched-scope failure on untouched, correctly-fixed code (T-2467's own T-2450 8-line-insert incident, reproduced on demand by Claude/Poirot/6597903-t2472-ask5-tracka-confirmation.md Sec4). `required_token_scope_end_offsets` (T-2475, keyed by `"relative/path.ext:occurrence_ordinal"`, occurrence_ordinal = this site's Nth marker found in this file) closed that drift but introduced a narrower one: ordinal depends on FILE ORDER, and Claude/Mendeleev/t2480-census-recommissioning-2026-08-31.md F1 constructed a genuinely producible edit -- REORDERING two of GS-10's own existing occurrences in their shared file, nothing added or removed, marker count unchanged, Part 1 blind to it -- under which a real revert of the relocated occurrence's own fix produced BYTE-FOR-BYTE IDENTICAL census output to the untouched tree: the relocated occurrence silently borrowed its neighbor's own offset, which spilled past its own governed code into unrelated downstream context that coincidentally satisfied the required-token check, while the neighbor was checked against a too-narrow borrowed window that never reached its own, untouched code -- a genuine revert absorbed for free while an unrelated, correct line was cited. T-2481 (D-SLM5659) found this same exposure, independently, on GS-11 (offsets 6/1, the same two-occurrence shape as GS-10, omitted from the prior commissioning's own exposure list) before building the remedy against it, and GS-12's own nine-occurrence population surfaced a second failure mode during the same derivation pass: a bare code-prefix anchor for one occurrence (`std::vector<int8_t> q_rot(`) collided with an unrelated, UNMARKED declaration of the same shape in a different function once a reorder pulled it inside another occurrence's own claimed window -- closed by switching GS-12's own anchors to each occurrence's own explanatory comment text (T-2432's own authoring convention places one immediately below every marker), which is far more specific than a short code prefix and, being prose, is immune to any revert of the CODE line it explains. A FOURTH stored-coordinate keying was ruled out in advance of building one (D-SLM5659): the defect is not which position is stored, it is that ANY position -- a proxy for where an occurrence's own code sits -- drifts from that code the moment the file's own layout changes around it, independent of the code's own correctness. `required_token_scopes` keys on the code's own local CONTENT instead, which travels WITH the code when the file is reordered, so there is no position left in the key for a reorder to desync. GS-12's two `ctx_wide` occurrences (offset 3 each) legitimately share one registered anchor -- their local comment text is identical by construction (a copy-pasted explanation for equivalent code in two sibling functions) -- and matching either physical marker to that one shared record is harmless: misassigning between two occurrences whose own registered offset is identical changes nothing about what gets checked. An edit INSIDE one occurrence's own governed span (between its marker and its own required token) can still desync the offset -- unchanged from every prior scheme, and not the class any of them targets. census.py fails closed on drift (`MISSING required_token_scopes ENTRY` for a gs_id with no registered record in a file it has a marker in; `MISSING SCOPE ANCHOR` for a physical marker none of its site's own registered anchors match; `AMBIGUOUS SCOPE ANCHOR` for a marker matched by anchors that disagree on offset) rather than silently.
